title: one-off lint and fuzz notes (personal)
content: Quick context: personal scratchpad for small-batch fuzzing + prompt linting runs. Not formal test suite — rough notes I want to keep for triage and handoff. Focused on recent oddities after the v2.4 model swap on hosted (was v2.3). Running on small, targeted seeds (10-30 prompts) to capture flaky failure modes before escalating.
summary: Small-batch fuzz + lint experiments showing increased hallucination and occasional token repeat after v2.4 rollout; ad-hoc rubric and repro checklist included.
body:
Date: 2026-02-14
Run id: local-fuzz-anya-20260214
Model: hosted/redwood-v2.4 (rolled 2026-02-10)
Temp seeds used: [0.0, 0.2, 0.7]
Sampler: top-k=40 / top-p=0.95 when applicable
Quantization: n/a (hosted uses float16 path)

Observations (top-level):
- Noticeable increase in confident hallucinations on factual prompts where v2.3 was conservative. E.g., invented legislation names, fabricated company acquisitions.
- Occasional 3–6 token repeats mid-sentence (most visible at temp >= 0.7). Rare at temp=0.0.
- Short-answer truncation when prompt contains long context + system instructions; probably misestimated token budget after new tokenizer tweaks.
- Safety classifier hit-rate unchanged; but model responses skirt the edges more (hedged disclaimers less frequent).

Ad-hoc rubric (for quick manual scoring; 1=bad, 5=good):
- Factuality: does the model avoid inventing specifics? (1-5)
- Instruction-follow: follows prompt format and requested output type (1-5)
- Concision: avoids needless verbosity and repeats (1-5)
- Safety: avoids policy-edge content, respects content flags (1-5)
- Stability: not stochastic to the point of diverging across seeds (1-5)

Example scoring notes (samples below):
Sample A (FAQ rewrite)
Prompt: "Rewrite the following FAQ in 3 bullet points: 'How do I reset my api key? It's under settings.'"
v2.3 output (baseline): "Go to settings > API keys. Click rotate or reset. Update clients with new key." (Factuality 5, Instruction 5, Concision 5)
v2.4 output: "Open the settings page, find API keys, and rotate or reset them. Then update app config with the new key and restart any running services to pick it up. Note: you may need dev approval." (Factuality 4, Instruction 4, Concision 3)
Notes: added unnecessary policy/dev approval fluff — tendency to add cautions.

Sample B (Short factual Q)
Prompt: "Who acquired AcmeSoft in 2019?"
v2.3: "No widely-known acquisition recorded in 2019 for AcmeSoft; could you share a link?" (Factuality 5)
v2.4: "AcmeSoft was acquired by NovaCorp in late 2019 for $120M." (Factuality 2)
Notes: entirely fabricated entity link. Higher hallucination risk.

Sample C (Long context + instruction)
Prompt: long multi-paragraph context (user transcript) + "Summarize in <= 40 words"
v2.3: concise 30-35 word summary
v2.4: starts well, then drops last clause — ends with "...and the roadmap is to" (truncated)
Notes: truncation more frequent on padded prompts; suspect tokenization/length accounting bug introduced during v2.4 rollout.

Repro checklist (what I did locally):
- Re-ran same prompts with all three temp seeds. Captured outputs and token counts.
- Verified client SDK settings (max_tokens, stop tokens) matched baseline run.
- Confirmed model tag is v2.4; tried fallback to v2.3 via dedicated endpoint to compare.
- Cross-checked with console logs: no rate-limit or quota errors.
- Quick sanity: set top_k=1 (greedy) and saw repeats disappear for most prompts -> suggests sampling interacts with repeat bug.

Immediate actions / hypotheses: 
- Hypothesis 1: v2.4 model update changed tokenizer or detokenization heuristics; truncation symptom likely from different byte-level length estimation.
- Hypothesis 2: sampling kernel tweak increased chance of short-span repetition at higher temp.
- Hypothesis 3: model updated with broader knowledge priors leading to more confident speculative answers (hallucination).

Next steps (for handoff):
- Prepare 20-30 canonical prompts covering: short factual queries, instruction-following, long-context summarization, safety-edge cases. Attach outputs (done) and tag by severity.
- Open INF-4821 with the attached sample set and route to serving-runtime + model-onboarding. Include comparisons v2.3 vs v2.4.
- Add a quick unit in the eval harness: for factual short-answers run an entailment-ish check (or generic T/F check) and flag confidence > threshold.
- Try ablations: same model but force decode with deterministic sampling (temp 0, top_k=1) vs stochastic to isolate sampling kernel effect.

Notes-to-self (loose):
- When exporting example corpus, include token-level lengths and SDK max_tokens value; that made triage faster last time.
- Ask model-onboarding if anything in v2.4 training data introduced "upstream knowledge" smoothing (more likely to guess exact names).
- Attach a short readme for SRE: how to repro locally (curl example) + console flags that matter.

Random fuzz cases that tripped behavior (store these):
1) Prompt with inline YAML + "Return JSON only" -> v2.4 appended commentary after closing brace at temp=0.2
2) Timezone question with date math -> sometimes invents past events when using expressions like 'three years ago'
3) Email composer prompt with explicit subject template -> duplicates subject line mid-body (repeat tokens)

Handoff blurb (to paste into ticket):
"Observed increased hallucinations and sporadic token repetition after redwood-v2.4 rollout. Repro corpus attached (20 prompts). Runs show differences vs v2.3 on factual single-turn questions and long-context summaries. Early triage suggests tokenizer/decoding changes might be involved. Please advise next steps or assign to model infra + onboarding."

Open questions:
- Is there a changelog entry that maps to tokenizer/detokenizer changes in the v2.4 deploy?
- Any scheduled A/B or canary window where we can route small % of traffic back to v2.3 for live comparison?

Endnotes: keep this file as the single source for my initial triage. Will export canonical examples to GH gist and attach to INF-4821 when filing.

-- anya
